title: Verify the rendered order when two downloadable resource items share the same Display Order value
description: Edge from step 4 — invalid/ambiguous combination. Both 'Research Proposal Template' and 'Research Proposal Guidelines' are given Display Order 1. The PBI states no tie-break rule (A-11).
steps_list: Set the Display Order of both 'Research Proposal Template' and 'Research Proposal Guidelines' to 1 and attempt to save the record
If the save is accepted, publish the record and open the published English page in a fresh logged-out browser context
Reload the page three times and record the order of the two resource cards on each load
expected_list: The system behaves deterministically: either the duplicate value is rejected with a validation message identifying the conflict, or both items are accepted
If accepted and published, both cards render — neither item is silently dropped and no card renders twice
The two cards appear in the same relative order on all three reloads; the order does not vary between renders

title: Verify the rendering of an Active information group whose every bullet is Inactive
description: Edge from step 4 — invalid combination across two objects. The 'Supporting information' group stays Active while all four of its bullets are set Inactive.
steps_list: Set the Active Status of all four bullets in the 'Supporting information' group to Inactive while leaving the group itself Active, and publish the record
Open the published English page in a fresh logged-out browser context and read section 02
Inspect the vertical space between the group intro and the start of the Downloadable resources section
expected_list: The record saves and publishes with the Liferay generic success toast

The group label 'Supporting information' and its intro 'Relevant supporting materials may be included to provide additional context for the proposed research topic.' render with no bullet list beneath them
No empty bullet markers, placeholder rows or blank vertical gap are left where the four bullets used to be; the Downloadable resources section follows the group intro directly

title: Verify the published page behaviour when a resource PDF is deleted from Documents and Media after publishing
description: Edge from step 4 — asset lifecycle diverging from the record that points at it. QCTEST-130949-template.pdf is deleted from Documents & Media while the resource item stays Active on the published page.
steps_list: Publish the page with the 'Research Proposal Template' card pointing at QCTEST-130949-template.pdf and confirm the download works in a logged-out context
Delete QCTEST-130949-template.pdf from Liferay Documents & Media, confirming the target by its exact file name before deleting
Reload the published English page in a fresh logged-out browser context and click the 'Download' button on the 'Research Proposal Template' card
expected_list: The download returns QCTEST-130949-template.pdf with HTTP 200 before the deletion
The file is positively identified by name and removed from Documents & Media

The visitor is not left with a silent failure: either the card no longer offers a download, or the click returns a handled not-found response rather than an unhandled server error; the rest of the page, including the second resource card, still renders and its download still works

title: Verify that a visitor holding the page open receives the replacement document and its updated size after a live document swap
description: Edge from step 4 — interrupted/concurrent transition and recovery. A logged-out visitor loads the published page; the Editor then replaces QCTEST-130949-template.pdf (200 KB) with QCTEST-130949-template-v2.pdf (1.2 MB) without unpublishing.
steps_list: In a logged-out browser context, load the published English page and leave it open on section 03 without reloading
In a separate Control Panel session, replace the file on the 'Research Proposal Template' item with QCTEST-130949-template-v2.pdf and save, keeping the page status Published
Without reloading, click the 'Download' button in the still-open visitor context
Reload the visitor page and read the first resource card's metadata, then click 'Download' again
expected_list: The visitor context shows the first resource card with 'PDF' and '200 KB'
The replacement saves with the Liferay generic success toast and the page status remains Published throughout
The click from the stale page does not produce an unhandled error — it returns either the new QCTEST-130949-template-v2.pdf or a handled not-found response, never a broken or truncated file
After reload the card reads 'PDF' and '1.2 MB' and the download returns QCTEST-130949-template-v2.pdf; the file type and file size shown match the file actually served
